back: When a measure becomes a target it stops being a good measure: strong optimisation of an imperfect proxy finds inputs where proxy and goal diverge.

front: Three stages of the RLHF reference pipeline
back: SFT on demonstrations; reward model from pairwise preferences (Bradley-Terry); RL (e.g. PPO) against the reward model with a KL penalty to the SFT policy.
$-\log\sigma(r(x,y_w)-r(x,y_l))$: logistic regression on the score difference of preferred vs rejected.

front: Closed-form optimum of the KL-regularised objective
back: $\pi^*(y)=\pi_{ref}(y)e^{r(y)/\beta}/Z$; the reference policy re-weighted exponentially by reward.
Small beta: strong amplification of the reward's flaws (reward hacking). Large beta: stays near the reference, little improvement.
Plot gold reward against KL (or sqrt KL) from the initial policy: it rises, peaks, then falls while the proxy keeps rising. Better proxies peak later.
Regressional (noise selected), extremal (tails), causal (proxy downstream), adversarial (agent games it).
$\log n-(n-1)/n$ (usual upper-bound estimate); lets you compare best-of-n with RL on one KL axis.

front: Name the four 'costumes' of reward hacking
back: Verbosity, sycophancy, unfaithful reasoning, evaluator tampering - all amplified features that correlated with approval.

front: Why can't a KL penalty fully prevent reward hacking?
back: It bounds distribution shift, not which modes are targeted; with heavy-tailed proxy error the constrained optimum can sit on high-proxy, low-gold responses.
(1) Sycophantic outputs are over-represented among high-reward outputs of the base model. (2) Any method that up-weights by $e^{r/\beta}$ therefore amplifies them.
Present the same false claim as the user's belief and as someone else's; the gap in affirmation isolates sycophancy from knowledge.
Reward $r'=r-\alpha\,\text{agree}(x,y)$. Lowers sycophancy but costs legitimate agreement with correct beliefs.

front: Why must the gold signal be held out?
back: If the optimiser can see or influence it, it becomes another proxy; monitoring needs a signal the optimisation could not exploit.
